headline: Anterior Poliomyelitis in Kentucky During 1935
source: American Journal of Public Health and the Nations Health (PubMed Central)
blurb: This article by A. T. McCormack and Fred W. Caudill on polio in Kentucky during 1935 was read at a public health meeting in St. Louis in November 1935 and printed in February 1936.

headline: 214.036 Exceptions to testing or immunization requirement.
blurb: This Kentucky law, created in 1962 and last amended in 2021, says a child does not have to be immunized when a health care provider writes that it would harm the child's health or when parents object on religious grounds in a sworn statement.

headline: A waterborne outbreak of hepatitis A in Meade County, Kentucky
source: American Journal of Public Health (PubMed Central)
blurb: Health officials in Meade County noticed a sudden rise in hepatitis A in November 1982, and a study of 73 cases found the biggest risk factor was household use of untreated water from one spring.

headline: Outbreaks of Pertussis Associated with Hospitals --- Kentucky, Pennsylvania, and Oregon, 2003
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: In August 2003, a 2-month-old infant in a Kentucky hospital nursery and a doctor who examined the infant both tested positive for whooping cough, and 72 exposed patients and 72 health care workers were given a preventive antibiotic.

headline: Acute Hepatitis A Outbreak – Cases Reported in Multiple Counties
source: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services
blurb: The Kentucky Department for Public Health declared a hepatitis A outbreak after 31 cases were reported across the state in 2017, a 50% increase over the 10-year average of 20 cases a year.

headline: 902 KAR 2:060. Immunization schedules for attending child day care centers, certified family child care homes, other licensed facilities which care for children, preschool programs, and public and private primary and secondary schools.
blurb: This Kentucky regulation's immunization schedule took effect for the school year starting on or after July 1, 2018, and it lists two doses of hepatitis A vaccine among the shots for children ages 5 and 6.

headline: Health Officials Announce Measles Outbreak in Central Kentucky
source: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services
blurb: Kentucky health officials said a measles outbreak that started in Woodford County had spread to Fayette County, with five measles cases in the state at the time and four of them tied to the outbreak.
